name: Willow
tagline: Push-to-talk dictation that transcribes your speech and cleans it up into finished text in whatever app you are typing in.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The pipeline here is not a secret: capture audio on a hotkey, run speech to text, run a small cleanup pass to strip the ums and fix punctuation, paste into the focused app. An agent can wire that up in a session with Whisper locally or an API, and for long-form writing it will feel about 80 percent as good. The last 20 percent is the part people actually pay for: sub-second latency, correct spelling of your coworkers and your codebase, not mangling the text when you paste into a terminal versus a Slack box, and never eating a recording. You will also be doing your own macOS accessibility permission dance and there is no mobile or keyboard-extension story at all. Buildable, genuinely useful, and you will feel every millisecond of the gap.
coreLoopDIY: A menu bar daemon that records while you hold a hotkey, transcribes it, runs an LLM cleanup pass with your custom vocabulary, and pastes the result into whatever window is focused.
requirements: macOS with microphone and accessibility permissions granted to the terminal or app running the daemon
Either a local Whisper model (a few GB, faster on Apple Silicon) or an API key for hosted speech to text
An LLM API key for the cleanup pass, or a local model if you want it fully offline
Willingness to debug global hotkey and simulated-paste behavior per app
whatYouLose: Latency tuning: hosted dictation apps stream audio and start transcribing before you stop talking, a naive build waits for the whole clip
Learned vocabulary that quietly absorbs your names, jargon and acronyms over months of use
Per-app formatting smarts, plain text for a terminal, formatted prose for a doc, short casual tone for chat
Reliability engineering: no dropped recordings, no half-pasted text, no dead hotkey after the laptop sleeps
Mobile and iPad dictation, plus a signed installable app instead of a Python process you babysit
moatNotes: Speech to text is a commodity API now. The defensible part is the hundred small decisions between the microphone and the cursor, plus the vocabulary the product learns about you.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because dictation is a reflex tool, and reflex tools have to work every single time or you stop reaching for them. A homemade version that hangs for two seconds, or types your colleague's name wrong, or silently fails once a day, gets abandoned in a week even though it technically works. Paying means someone else owns the latency, the model swaps, the OS permission changes and the edge case where you dictate into a password field. That is a small monthly fee against a habit you use fifty times a day.
notes: The transcription is free, the flinch-free feel is not.
prompt:
Build a local push-to-talk dictation daemon for macOS. No accounts, no telemetry, no cloud storage of audio.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Python 3.12, managed with uv, single package `dictate`
- sounddevice + numpy for microphone capture at 16kHz mono
- faster-whisper for local transcription, default model `small.en`, configurable via .env
- pynput for a global hotkey listener
- pyobjc (AppKit) for clipboard writes, and a simulated Cmd+V keystroke to paste
- rumps for a minimal menu bar item (status, toggle cleanup, quit)
- httpx for the optional LLM cleanup call

Behavior:
- Hold Right Option to record, release to stop. Show a menu bar state change while recording.
- On release: transcribe locally, then if CLEANUP=1 send the transcript to an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint with a strict prompt that only removes filler words, fixes punctuation and capitalization, and applies a user vocabulary list. It must never answer, summarize, or add content.
- Load vocabulary from `vocab.txt`, one term per line, and inject it into both the Whisper initial_prompt and the cleanup prompt.
- Write the final text to the clipboard, restore the previous clipboard contents after 5 seconds, and paste into the focused app.
- If anything fails, paste the raw transcript rather than nothing, and log the error.

Also include:
- `.env.example` with OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL, WHISPER_MODEL, CLEANUP, HOTKEY
- A local SQLite history file storing timestamp, raw transcript and cleaned transcript, with a `dictate history` command and a `dictate purge` command
- Audio kept in memory only, never written to disk
- README with the exact macOS Accessibility and Microphone permission steps, and a note that first run downloads the model

Out of scope: streaming partial transcripts, iOS, cross-platform support, multi-language, speaker diarization, any hosted backend.
